direct_answer: Shoulder osteoarthritis can make washing, dressing and reaching difficult. Simple changes, equipment such as long-handled sponges and dressing sticks, gentle exercises and advice from an occupational therapist can help.
author: Louis Maxwell
reviewer_credentials: First Contact Practitioner, HCPC PH128483, CSP member

content:
Painful shoulders make everyday self-care harder.

This guide covers practical tips. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Washing

  • Long-handled sponges.
  • A seat in the shower.
  • Lever taps.

Dressing

  • Dress the painful arm first.
  • Use front-opening clothes.
  • Dressing sticks.

Reaching high cupboards

  • Keep items at waist height.
  • Use a reacher.
  • Avoid climbing.

Exercises and help

A physiotherapist can suggest gentle exercises; an occupational therapist can advise on equipment.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Will exercise help?

Gentle exercise can help.

Where can I get equipment?

Ask your council or OT.
